items.quote: This document sets out the University of Northern British Columbia’s Policy and Response Procedures for allegations of Sexual Violence or Misconduct.
items.reason: The policy is a stand-alone document with its own dedicated response procedures.
The policy does not commit to being publicly posted or available.

items.quote: Members of the University Community who wish to make a Sexual Violence or Misconduct Report should contact the Response and Support Team at www.unbc.ca/sexual-violence.
items.reason: The policy provides clear, concrete steps on how and where to make a report.
The policy does not address the complainant's past sexual history.
The policy does not guarantee protection from face-to-face contact with the respondent.

items.quote: Survivors/persons affected by Sexual Violence or Misconduct are free to tell the story of their own experiences.
items.reason: The policy explicitly states that survivors are free to share their own experiences.

items.quote: Survivors/persons affected by Sexual Violence or Misconduct are entitled to choose the process that is best for them.
items.reason: The policy explicitly guarantees the survivor's right to choose their preferred reporting process.
The policy does not mention amnesty for drug or alcohol use when reporting.

items.quote: The University will promptly respond to Reports of Sexual Violence or Misconduct made under this or any other University Policy.
items.reason: The policy uses vague timeline terms like 'promptly' rather than setting specific binding deadlines.

items.quote: Where the University receives information that requires it to act to protect the health and safety of the Members of the University Community, or University property, the University may impose interim measures before an investigation is concluded.
items.reason: Interim measures are discretionary as the policy states the university 'may' impose them.

items.quote: At an event or during an activity sponsored or under the auspices of the University, including but not limited to the following: i. Athletic events ii. Field schools iii. Distance and online courses iv. Co-op, internships and practicum placements
items.reason: The policy's scope explicitly covers co-op, internships, and practicum placements.

items.quote: The complainant has the right to know the outcome of the investigation, but not the details of any disciplinary actions that may have been taken against the respondent unless disclosing that information is necessary for health or safety reasons or because it affects the Survivor/person affected by Sexual Violence or Misconduct.
items.reason: The policy commits to informing the complainant of the outcome, including relevant disciplinary actions if they affect the survivor.

items.quote: The President will provide information to the Board of Governors each year on the implementation of the Policy.
items.reason: The policy requires annual reporting, but it is internal to the Board of Governors rather than public.

items.quote: The University is committed to reviewing the Policy at least once every three years and/or when directed to do so by the Minister of Advanced Education.
items.reason: The policy requires a review cycle of every three years rather than every two years.
The policy does not mandate student representation on policy review committees.

items.quote: Response and Support Team – a small team of highly trained Members of the University Community who have been selected based on their experience.
items.reason: Training is mentioned for the response team, but it is not explicitly required to be trauma-informed.

items.quote: Coordinating education and training programs pertaining to preventing and responding to incidents of Sexual Violence and Misconduct for the Members of the University Community.
items.reason: The university commits to coordinating prevention education and training programs for the university community.
